production_calls.observation: The writer flush reads the full not-yet-stored suffix, appends it to its owned handle, then advances storedCount by the accepted batch length. A concurrently appended event stays beyond the cursor for a later flush.

The synchronous pre-dispatch invariant scans for step/start and folds request/header before comparing the immutable request with Session.deriveMessages(). Session.requestHeader() already maintains the header fold, and AgentLoop's turnBoundary projection already tracks lastStepStartSeq.

SystemPromptProjection repeatedly reads active surface nodes and resolves each node through eventAt() to recover the system-message text needed for append, replacement, clear, and series-reset decisions.

RuntimeContextProjection scans the full log newest-first at construction, then watches committed events to retain or clear the latest system-prompt-owned user snapshot. The restore path selects the latest still-visible owned message.

prepared_session_lifecycle.observed: AgentLoop.create/createAgent/resume prepare an unpublished Session and construct ReactLoopAgent before SessionStore.enter/announce. SessionProjectionRegistry initializes live cells from session/created or explicit hydrate, so stateOf(turnBoundary) can fail during Agent construction before either initializer runs.
prepared_session_lifecycle.consequence: A prepared-session baseline and prepublication append path must initialize and advance projections before Agent construction and setup. Publication must not expose the Session before its initial persistence batch is accepted.

unpublished_reader_constraints.observed: SessionQuery resolves live Sessions through ctx.sessions and cold history through sessionPersistence. The fresh Session is not in the live store before publication; a newly created write handle owns writes and does not provide a safe independent query path for the unpublished in-memory suffix.
unpublished_reader_constraints.consequence: Do not replace S020 with a SessionQuery read, publish the Session early, or add another synchronous arbitrary-history alias.

session_projections.observed: SessionProjectionRegistry already supports exact restore/hydrate cuts, eager pure folds, host-only JSON state, and per-cell sequence watermarks. Cache restoration falls back to a full event read when a new projection key has no usable checkpoint row.

shared_prepublication_source.decision: Add one SessionPreparation-owned event source that carries the exact constructor baseline and every accepted append until publication. The source exposes ordered bounded asynchronous pages through a fixed inclusive watermark, cancellation, and a committed sequence cursor; it is lifecycle-scoped rather than a general Session history API.

owners.definition_and_provider: dsh-session owns the exact prepared baseline and captures accepted appends before the Session is announced.
owners.projection_consumer: dsh-session-projection initializes each registered cell from the prepared baseline and advances it from captured appends; after announcement, its sequence watermark suppresses duplicate session/event delivery.
owners.persistence_consumer: dsh-agent-loop drains pages into its owned SessionHandle before publication; it advances storedCount only after append resolves, then hands later committed events to the existing backend live route.

preserved_behavior: Fresh, seeded, forked, and resumed Sessions persist the complete ordered log from seq 0 exactly once; inheritedEventCount remains separate lineage metadata.
Resume starts the stored cursor after the cold-read prefix and synthetic crash-repair closers, then includes setup-time appends.
Events committed while a page append is pending remain visible after the fixed watermark and are drained before publication or routed after publication without gaps or duplicates.

A page advances its source and storage cursors only after the corresponding handle append succeeds; failure, cancellation, or owner disposal prevents publication and releases the handle and preparation.
An empty fresh Session still follows existing materialization behavior; no seed marker or Session log event is invented.
rejected_paths: SessionQuery cannot address the not-yet-published in-memory Session and would not capture setup-time events.
Entering or announcing the Session before persistence accepts its constructor/setup prefix would make an incomplete Session observable.
A new synchronous Session reader would retain the residency dependency forbidden by the active deprecation decision.
gate_conditions: The source has one immutable cut per drain, preserves contiguous seq order and inherited-prefix metadata, and bounds each returned page.
The final prepublication drain and live writer handoff have one observable ordering point with no missed or duplicated event under concurrent append and cancellation.
Fresh create, createAgent setup, seeded create, resume repair, append rejection, cancellation, owner unload, retry-after-failure, and immediate post-publication append are falsifying cases.

request_invariant.decision: Keep the llm/stream check synchronous and fail-closed. Use session.requestHeader() for the latest canonical header, session.deriveMessages() for the current message projection, and the initialized turnBoundary.lastStepStartSeq for the step/start precondition; remove the event scan and foldRequestHeader call from the invariant.
preserved_behavior: Loop requests still require frozen options, a live Session id, frozen messages, at least one step/start, an existing request/header, exact message equality, and matching request-header fields before the provider dispatches.
Missing projection state is an explicit load-order or lifecycle failure, never treated as an empty Session.
falsifying_cases: No step/start and no request/header fail synchronously.
Open-step context included in deriveMessages passes; unlogged prefixes, suffixes, or message divergence fail.
Header model, system, temperature, maxTokens, stop, or tools divergence fails before the provider is entered.
A fresh unpublished Session and a resumed Session have the exact projection baseline before the invariant runs.

system_prompt_projection.decision: Replace repeated surface-node eventAt lookups with a host-only projection of active system/message nodes in surface order. Apply append and replacement operations using the accepted surface range; retain the current empty-content and non-single-text distinctions used by SystemPromptProjection.
preserved_behavior: The system prompt remains surface node 0 and in-history replacements still normalize surviving versions.
Plain routes, broken request series, empty rendered prompts, unchanged prompts, and capable continuing series keep their current append/replacement decisions.
No model-visible prompt is changed by projection restoration alone.
falsifying_cases: Seeded/resumed system head plus active tails restore in the exact surface order.
A replacement range that shadows system nodes removes exactly those nodes; appends preserve later active nodes.
Empty and multi-block messages retain their distinct current text classifications.
Projection state and current request derivation agree before and after compact/retry paths.

runtime_context_projection.decision: Replace the reverse history scan with a host-only projection of the latest active user/message owned by `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt`, updated from committed surface events and seeded from the exact prepared baseline.
runtime_context_projection.restore_semantics: The existing cold constructor chooses the latest still-visible owned message. Make live updates converge to that same active-surface result when a replacement shadows the newest snapshot but an earlier owned snapshot remains visible.
preserved_behavior: Other sessions, non-owned messages, and log-only events do not alter the retained runtime-context value.
No snapshot ever remains distinct from an explicit cleared marker, and non-single-text content remains distinct from empty text.
The projection only suppresses or proposes the existing system-prompt-owned user/message; that model-visible event remains logged through the existing append path.
falsifying_cases: The latest owned snapshot remains unchanged after unrelated events and session traffic.
Replacement of the latest owned node selects the newest older owned node still on the active surface, matching restore behavior.
Replacement of every owned node produces the cleared state; a new owned snapshot replaces it.
Live, seeded, and resumed projection states agree for the same durable events.

compatibility.decision: No SessionEventMap member, SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION, released Session record, persistence schema, wire field, or provider request field changes. Host-only projection rows remain derived cache state; old rows missing new keys must refold from seq 0 and produce the same state.

Scoped typecheck, lint, package dependency, type-equivalence, API/catalog/module-graph, bilingual README/doc checks, ownership, direct-reader count, and whitespace gates.
